```{r setup}
library(Lab4)
```

# Divide the BostonHousing data into a test and training dataset using the caret package.
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(caret)
data("BostonHousing", package = "mlbench")

set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(BostonHousing$medv, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)

train_boston <- BostonHousing[train_index, ]
test_boston <- BostonHousing[-train_index, ]

```

# Fit a linear regression model and a fit a linear regression model with forward selection of covariates on the training dataset.

## Linear regression model
```{r}
set.seed(123)
linreg_mod1 <- train(medv~., data = train_boston, method = "lm")
```

## Linear regression model with forward selection 

NOTE: Not sure about this solution, the built-in 'leapForward' method in caret requrires at least one covariate. Might have to create a 
custom function but...
```{r}
null_model <- lm(medv~1, data = train_boston)
forward_linreg <- train(medv~1 + ., data = train_boston, 
                        method = "leapForward", 
                        tuneGrid = expand.grid(nvmax = 0:(ncol(train_boston)-1)),
                        trControl = trainControl(method = "cv",number = 10), metric = "RMSE")

summary(forward_linreg)
```

# Evaluate the performance of this model on the training dataset.

The full linear model and forward selection model perform similarly. 
```{r}
pred_lm <- predict(linreg_mod1, newdata = train_boston)
pred_null <- predict(null_model)
pred_forward <- predict(forward_linreg$finalModel, newdata = train_boston)

knitr::kable(rbind(postResample(pred_lm, train_boston$medv),
postResample(pred_null, train_boston$medv),
postResample(pred_forward, train_boston$medv)), col.names = c("LM model", "Intercept-only", "Forward Selection"))
```

#  Fit a ridge regression model using your ridgereg() function to the training dataset for different values of lambda

## Create custom model for ridge regression 
```{r}
ridge_caret <- list(
  label = "Custom Ridge Regression",
  library = NULL,
  type = "Regression",
  
  parameters = data.frame(
    parameter = "lambda",
    class = "numeric",
    label = "Lambda"
  ),
  
  grid = function(x, y, len = NULL, search = "grid") {
    data.frame(
      lambda = 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = len)
    )
  },
  
  fit = function(x, y, wts, param, lev, last, classProbs, ...) {
    
    dat <- data.frame(.outcome = y, x)
    
    ridgereg(
      formula = .outcome ~ .,
      data = dat,
      lambda = param$lambda
    )
  },
  
  predict = function(modelFit, newdata, submodels = NULL) {
    newdata <- as.data.frame(newdata)
    predict(modelFit, newdata = newdata)
  },
  
  prob = NULL
)
```

## Fit the model over grid of different lambda
```{r}
lambda_grid <- expand.grid(
  lambda = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000)
)

set.seed(123)
ridge_model <- train(
  x = train_boston[, names(train_boston) != "medv"],
  y = train_boston$medv,
  method = ridge_caret,
  tuneGrid = lambda_grid,
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = "cv",
    number = 10
  ),
  metric = "RMSE"
)
```


# Find the best hyperparameter value for lambda using 10-fold cross-validation on the training set
```{r}
set.seed(123)
lambda_grid <- expand.grid(
  lambda = seq(from = 1e-3, to = 1e2, by = 1e-1)
)
ridge_model_2 <- train(
  x = train_boston[, names(train_boston) != "medv"],
  y = train_boston$medv,
  method = ridge_caret,
  tuneGrid = lambda_grid,
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = "cv",
    number = 10
  ),
  metric = "RMSE"
)
pred_ridge <- predict(ridge_model_2, newdata = train_boston)
paste0("Best lambda: ", ridge_model_2$bestTune)
postResample(
  pred = pred_ridge,
  obs = train_boston$medv
)
```

# Evaluate the performance of all three models on the test dataset and write some concluding comments.

Conclusion: forward selection model appears to give the best RMSE. The normal lm model and ridge regesssion model both preform very similarly. 
```{r}
lm_test <- predict(linreg_mod1, newdata = test_boston) %>% postResample(obs = test_boston$medv)
forward_test <- predict(forward_linreg, newdata = test_boston) %>% postResample(obs = test_boston$medv)
ridge_test <- predict(ridge_model_2, newdata = test_boston) %>% postResample(obs = test_boston$medv)

knitr::kable(data.frame(rbind(lm_test, forward_test, ridge_test)))
```
